start_pursuit.ask: What are the milestones, and which of them have dates?

learn.ask: What do they want to be able to do, and by when?

gate: 2-3 diagnostic questions before teaching: ask_user, then update_plan(fields={'baseline': ...})
learn.ask: Before teaching anything: 2-3 questions on what they already know.

gate: read what the library holds, then choose the focus concepts: update_plan(fields={'focus': [...]})
learn.ask: What does the library hold on this, and which concepts should this session focus on?
Ask one question anchored in a source passage; the person answers; feedback cites the passage; record what they understand.

gate: let them explain it in their own words, critique it against the sources, then understanding_record and update_plan(fields={'consolidated': ...})
learn.ask: Let the person explain it in their own words first; critique it against the sources, grounded like the scribe.

gate: review dates as tasks - task_add(note='<project note>', text='Review: <concept>', due=..., heading='Understanding') - or enable the Spaced Repetition plugin, then update_plan(fields={'scheduled': ...})
learn.ask: When should this be reviewed again, and is there a next session to propose?

gate: name the candidate: update_plan(fields={'candidate': ...}) - a curated server (capability_candidates) or a repository URL the person gave
add_capability.ask: Which server? One from capability_candidates (the curated list), or a repository URL the person gives - never one found by browsing on your own.

gate: ingest the candidate's repository, so it is read as a source

before committing: record what you are assuming and how each was settled - record_assumptions([{assumption, settled_by, how}]), where settled_by is a tool you called here, an answered question's id, or 'unverifiable' (an empty list if you assume nothing)
add_capability.ask: ingest its repository, read it as a source, and record the assessment: licence, maintenance, what it claims, caveats, what it can reach - its card is its own claim, and the narrowest tool that does the job is the one to want.

gate: propose its exact definition: capability_propose(...)
add_capability.ask: Propose one exact, pinned definition: which launcher, which version, which secrets (as ${ENV} names only), and why this library needs it.

gate: capability_install(name) - it asks the person; a decline is a finished outcome too
add_capability.ask: The person decides: capability_install asks them, and installs only on yes.
What did the library fail to answer?

gate: no requirements yet: the person sets them with set_requirement
audited.ask: Which open requirement comes next, and what one bounded step serves it? Record it with update_plan(fields={'proposal': {'requirements': [...], 'step': ...}}); ask the person instead if the requirement is unclear.

gate: no contract has been admitted: preflight admits one

gate: no contract has been admitted: preflight admits one
audited.ask: Do only what the admitted contract allows, through its tools.

gate: no contract has been admitted: preflight admits one
audited.ask: Tier A checks every predicate of the contract's requirements on the actual artifacts; a missing or failed check is recorded, not skipped.

gate: no contract has been admitted: preflight admits one
audited.ask: The Core turns the round's results into requirement statuses. Then start the next round, or close the session if every requirement is accounted for.

workflows.name: deep-read-staged
workflows.purpose: read the whole text of every staged source, part by part - claims and limits with their pages, terms, and any reasoning stance a text teaches, staged as a lens (V1's lens scan, on the clerk channel)

workflows.name: draft-reflection
workflows.purpose: draft a short reflection grounded only in a week's own gathered tasks, activity and desk (W3 weekly-review, step 4)

workflows.name: flag-sensitive
workflows.purpose: mark one staged source for a person's review as possibly dual-use

workflows.name: gather-activity
workflows.purpose: what was read and written across every session - or one pursuit's, given a project - since a cutoff (W3 weekly-review, step 2)

workflows.name: gather-agenda
workflows.purpose: every open, dated task across the vault - or one pursuit's, given a project - bucketed by when it falls (W3 weekly-review, step 1)

workflows.name: gather-desk
workflows.purpose: a pursuit's current working set (W3 weekly-review, step 3)

workflows.name: ingest-cited
workflows.purpose: record an external research report's cited links as evidence, then fetch and stage every cited arXiv or DOI paper (V1's ingest_resolved_links, declared)

workflows.name: review-conversation
workflows.purpose: find catalogued sources relevant to a snapshot of a conversation; writes nothing

workflows.name: review-due
workflows.purpose: open one parked learn session per concept whose review task is due, framed for the review, for the person to resume from Sessions (Co-work Roadmap §2 W4, §4 D4)

workflows.name: review-item
workflows.purpose: draft the unframed Bottom Line and run the sensitivity check for one staged source

workflows.name: review-staged
workflows.purpose: draft the unframed Bottom Line and run the sensitivity check for every staged source that has none yet (V1's draft_staging_promotions, declared)

workflows.name: run-queue
workflows.purpose: take what is waiting in the intake queue through fetch, evidence, description and staging

workflows.name: sync-vault
workflows.purpose: keep the vault's ignore rules current, commit what changed, and push it

pipelines.name: clear-enrichment-backlog
pipelines.purpose: run the intake queue, then route each fetched source to review, a sensitivity flag, or nothing further

pipelines.name: weekly-review
pipelines.purpose: gather a pursuit's tasks, cross-session activity and desk, then draft a reflection for the person to review (Co-work Roadmap §2, W3)

macros.name: review_staged_candidate
